text.p: Gold prices slumped to a 12 year low in late New York trade, sparked by Reseve Bank of Australia sales. Elsewhere, wheat and oil prices were lower, while base metal markets eased from early peaks but most finished higher. The CRB index was down 1.85 at 235.57.

Copper prices consolidated the late upmove seen on Wednesday with business in a broad $2,400/2,420 range. With backwardation rates for the full cash/threes backwardation and some of the sensitive July dates easing slightly, the market tended to gravitate towards the lower end of the band, traders said.

However, the bias remains to the upside, given the tightness from the July date to the end of July that will become prominent in the run-up to "third Wednesday". Last three months business was at $2,404, still up $14 from yesterday's kerb.
Zinc was unable to re-challenge its morning peak of $1,495 due to profit-taking following gains of some $150 in the last week. Prices ended at $1,476, up $13.
Traders see the downmove as fairly restricted, given forthcoming tightness later in the third quarter, with major shorts finding stocks tightly controlled.
Aluminium also stepped back from highs near $1,620 amid expectations of producer sales. However, there was reasonable buying near $1,600, and final trade at $1,605.50 was just $4.50 down.
Nickel prices drifted back towards the lower end of the day's range after early failing above $7,000 but final trade at $6,930 was only just $10 down from Wednesday.
Lead traded in a narrow, albeit steadier band, closing just below $640 at $639, up $7.
Tin was lacklustre, closing at $5,530, down $5 while alloy was quoted at $1,455/60.

GOLD - Gold prices slumped to a 12 year low in late pre-holiday New York trade, leading COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures to a lower close across the board, after news the Australian central bank had sold 167 tonnes of gold from reserves in recent months. "The Australian disposal was a forward sale arranged some time ago, with only the deliveries occurring now, so you could argue the market has already at least partly discounted it," Refco New York economist James Steel said. "But it confirms that central banks worldwide, not just European central banks, are mobilizing their gold reserves to achieve better returns," he said. COMEX August gold ended down $7.10 at $325.20 an ounce. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $325.00/50, after briefly seeing a low at $323.70 an ounce, just below a low around $325.10 seen in March 1993.

OIL - NYMEX oil prices settled sharply lower in an abbbreviated trading session on news Iraq was a step closer to resuming oil sales, dealers said. August crude finished 78 cents lower at $19.56 a barrel. "The market had gotten overdone and was due for a correction and that Iraq story had gotten the ball rolling," said Tom Bentz, energy analyst with High Yield Analytics in New York.

GRAINS - CBOT soft red winter wheat futures were lower on active harvest and on reports of excellent wheat yields, especially in the key U.S. hard red winter wheat state of Kansas, traders said. A new contract low of $3.27 per bushel was set in September, below the previous low of $3.29 set on Monday.
